LESSON: SENTENCE FORMATION

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Sentence formation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Sentence formation. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write a variety of compound 5 lessons 180 structures correctly correct punctuation, individually, in pairs and
2. develop strategies for making and organizing notes
3. use writing and other forms of representation to generate and organize ideas
4. appreciate the importance of logic in writing Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learners practice writing sentences and paragraphs in pairs and groups

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Sentence formation using something you see at school.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Sentence formation.
2. Explain Sentence formation to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Sentence formation.
4. Show that you can: write a variety of compound 5 lessons 180 structures correctly correct punctuation, individually, in pairs and
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Sentence formation. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Sentence formation important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. write a variety of compound 5 lessons 180 structures correctly correct punctuation, individually, in pairs and
